transcript:
Meeting header: 
- Date: 2028-11-02 09:23 PST
- Duration: 47m
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Asha Kapoor (CTO - Palisade), Liam O'Neill (Head of Security), Evan Park (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary: quick discovery to map security requirements; customer leaning toward dedicated or VPC private for low-latency teleop, but wants clarity on audits and KMS.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya with Redwood Inference, and diego's our solutions engineer — we'll run through your security needs and how hosting options map to them, quick intro?
[00:12] Asha: yeah hi, i'm asha, cto at palisade robotics, we build teleop + perception for industrial drones, so latency and data control are both big for us.
[00:22] Liam: liam — sec lead, primarily responsible for compliance and audit readiness. we need to know how keys, logs, and sso will work end to end.
[00:30] Diego: thanks — can you give us a short current state? like where models run today, any encryption/kms you use, idp?
[00:38] Evan: sure, today inference runs on-prem on a small pool of A100s, we store telemetry in s3, use AWS KMS CMKs, okta for SSO, SCIM not fully wired up yet. want to move to managed inference but worried about cost and latency tradeoffs.
[00:50] Maya: makes sense, so primary questions i expect are around SOC2/ISO proof, sso integration, k m s integration and whether you can bring your own keys, and audit logs + retention. anything else?
[00:59] Asha: also multi-tenant RBAC — we'll expose model endpoints internally to teams and need strict least-priv. and data residency for eu customers, possibly on prem later.
[01:10] Diego: got it. quick lay of options: hosted API is fastest to get going but has shared infra, dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for you with isolation and predictable perf, private (VPC/on-prem) gives you control over networking and key custody.
[01:26] Liam: for compliance, we need to know whether your hosted offering supports customer-managed keys or we must do dedicated/private to have BYOK.
[01:35] Maya: short answer: we support BYOK for Private deployments and for Dedicated via KMS integrations in your VPC; hosted we offer service-side encryption and a managed KMS model but we also have enterprise contracts for key escrow patterns — i'll attach the exact security pack.
[01:49] Evan: when you say "attach" — is that a public doc or do we need an NDA?
[01:53] Maya: SOC2 summary is public for prospects; detailed controls matrix we share under an NDA. i'll add links.
[02:00] Liam: what's your SOC2 scope? infrastructure only or application/data plane?
[02:05] Diego: our SOC2 Type II covers the control environment for the platform, ops, data handling, and incident response — we can map control families to your requirements.
[02:14] Asha: iso? any plans / cert?
[02:17] Maya: we have an ISO 27001 program in progress — i can share the status and expected timeline.
[02:21] [crosstalk] Evan: mm-hmm
[02:24] Diego: on SSO: we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, and role sync for RBAC. there are sometimes minor mapping issues with groups across idps — we typically handle group-to-role mapping in the console or via provisioning hooks.
[02:38] Liam: do you support session-level tokens and short-lived creds for audit?
[02:41] Diego: yes, sessions are short-lived, and audit logs show token issuance and key ops. logs stream to our observability system, and for Dedicated/Private we can forward logs into your SIEM via secure forwarders.
[02:53] Asha: how detailed are the audit logs? we want per-request model id, input hash, user, timestamp, response status, and which model variant served it.
[03:03] Diego: that's supported — we can emit per-request metadata, and you can configure retention. note: full input-text retention raises privacy concerns; we often recommend hashing inputs and storing payloads only in private deployments or with explicit retention policies.
[03:19] Liam: and for telemetry/kv cache — is anything persisted in the service? our concern is ephemeral KV cache containing session context.
[03:26] Maya: by default KV cache is ephemeral and stored in-memory; for performance we may spill to local SSDs on the serving hosts but we do not persist user payloads long-term unless configured. for private setups you can enforce no-disk persistence.
[03:41] Evan: about encryption — can we bring our own KMS (HSM-backed CMK) and have the platform use envelope encryption with client-side or server-side wrapping?
[03:50] Diego: yes, for Private we integrate your KMS; Dedicated in VPC also supports using your KMS via IAM roles and endpoint. hosted managed KMS is available but if BYOK is required we recommend Private.
[04:03] Asha: any dual-key schemes? like platform signs but we hold root?
[04:07] Diego: we do ecosystem patterns, double envelope for backups, and customer root CMK for key wrapping — we can sketch a diagram in the deep dive.
[04:15] Liam: retention — we need retention windows and deletion guarantees. do you support automated retention policies and verifiable deletions?
[04:23] Maya: yes, retention policies are configurable per tenant/route; for private you can enforce immediate purge. verifiable deletion: we provide deletion APIs and audit of deletion events; for full legal attestation we'd work with our legal team and can provide deletion certificates under contract.
[04:38] Evan: latency — when you say Dedicated, what's typical p99 for a 1k token model? in our current on-prem p99 is ~120ms for local calls — we can't accept p99 of 400ms for teleop control loops.
[04:50] Diego: fair — dedicated with GPU pooling in region can get p99 similar to on-prem if you provision adequate reserved capacity and keep KV caches warm; we'll need to benchmark with your prompt distribution. hosted multi-tenant can be slightly higher and has occasional tail, we have SLOs for enterprise tenants though.
[05:06] Asha: pricing tradeoffs — is dedicated monthly vs hosted per-token? and is there a hybrid where burst to hosted if dedicated saturated?
[05:14] Maya: yes. hosted is usage-based; dedicated is reserved commit with optional burst credits to hosted or higher tiers. we support smart routing to fall back to cheaper or higher-availability variants per policy.
[05:27] Liam: security question: where do audit logs live? are they encrypted at rest and can we push them to our cloud account?
[05:33] Diego: logs are encrypted at rest; for Dedicated/Private we can ship logs to your cloud account or SIEM via TLS-forwarder. encryption uses envelope keys and can be integrated with your KMS.
[05:45] Evan: can we run a short proof-of-concept with redwood, say 2-week pilot on dedicated with a small GPU pool and sample telemetry?
[05:52] Maya: absolutely. we'd do a scoped POC with acceptance criteria — usually latency, throughput, and logging/keys. diego will draft the POC success metrics.
[05:59] [10:00 minute mark omitted for brevity]
[10:02] Diego: a few notes on RBAC — we support tenant-level roles, route-level permissions, and granular API keys. you can restrict model-publish to admins and grant read-only to integrators.
[10:15] Asha: can we enforce separation between platform ops and data ops? like ops can manage infra but not see user payloads.
[10:22] Diego: yes, using role scoping and KMS separation we can model that. for extra isolation we recommend Private with distinct key material.
[10:31] Liam: incident response — what is your timeline for notifying customers?
[10:35] Maya: we commit to 24-hour initial notification for security incidents and 72-hour follow-up with remediation plan for critical incidents under enterprise contracts.
[10:44] Evan: is there a runbook we can review?
[10:46] Maya: yes, i'll include the IR runbook summary; detailed runbooks are shared under NDA.
[10:51] Asha: okay, procurement and legal will want SLA language and data processing addendum.
[10:55] Maya: noted — we'll provide standard DPA and SLA templates.
[11:00] Liam: curious about e-discovery and logs — if a regulator asks for a subset of requests, can you pull that and provide chain-of-custody?
[11:09] Diego: we keep immutable audit chains for enterprise customers and can export with timestamps and verification metadata; chain-of-custody may be contractually attested.
[11:18] Evan: one more: how do you handle model updates and rollbacks? we need an audit trail that ties a response to the exact model binary and config.
[11:25] Diego: each model version has a unique revision id, we record which variant served a request and store that in the audit event. rollouts support canary/A-B and automatic fallback; we'll provide traces.
[11:36] Asha: ok we're mostly comfortable with the feature set. our gating items are: have to see SOC2 controls matrix, confirm BYOK for dedicated/private, and run a latency bench.
[11:47] Maya: good list — so next steps recap: i'll send SOC2 & ISO status, diego will coordinate bench plan w/ evan, and we'll put together dedicated pricing and POC scope.
[11:58] Liam: timeline — we're aiming to choose a vendor by end of november, internal security review first week of december.
[12:06] Maya: understood — we'll prioritize getting materials to you this week so you can start the review.
[12:12] Evan: also, can you share the daily audit log format sample?
[12:15] Diego: yes, will share a sample with field names and retention knobs.
[12:19] Asha: great. anything else?
[12:22] Maya: that's it from us. thanks everyone. i'll send meeting notes and the security pack.

End meeting.
